This is the staged path through **OrgPath**, the governance member of the
Org family. Each stage names what to **read**, what to **do**, and how to
**verify** — the same discipline the [Contributor track](contributor-track.qmd)
uses. The path invents nothing: every stage sequences material that is
already published, per [ADR-131](../adr/adr-131-academy-org-family-umbrella.qmd).
The pillar's front door is the [OrgPath landing](../orgpath/index.qmd).

Before stage 1, open [Substrate Status](../docs/substrate-status.qmd) and
keep it open. It is the candid map of what is implemented, partial, and
aspirational — every claim you meet on this path can be checked against it.

---

## Stage 1 — See it work (the ten-minute loop)

**Read:** [OrgPath Governance Golden Path](../docs/orgpath-golden-path.qmd) —
AD facts → derived facets → drift classification → signed evidence, in four
commands, with no live AD, no Azure tenant, and no API keys.

**Do:** clone the repo and run the golden path on your own machine
(`examples/orgtree/golden-path/run.sh`; prerequisites are Python 3.10+ and
git). Everything is read-only or dry-run by default.

**Verify:** the run terminates in a signed evidence bundle with OSCAL
Assessment Results. If you can say what each of the four commands
(`assess`, `inventory`, `govern`, `orgtree-readiness-bundle`) proved, stage
1 is done.

## Stage 2 — The architecture (the addressing plane)

**Read:** the [Reference Architecture](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/index.qmd),
in this order: [OrgTree](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/orgtree.qmd)
(the organizational hierarchy), [LocPath](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/locpath.qmd)
(the location dimension), the
[codebook](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/codebook.qmd)
(paths bound to authoritative codes), and the
[OrgPath FAQ](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/orgpath-faq.qmd).
Then the runtime pages:
[drift walkthrough](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/drift-walkthrough.qmd),
[delegation](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/delegation.qmd), and
[dynamic groups](../customer-documents/reference-architecture/dynamic-groups.qmd).

**Do:** sketch your own organization's top two OrgTree levels and the
LocPath for one real site, following the codebook's binding rules.

**Verify:** you can answer, without looking: why is the OU tree not the
answer; what makes a path *governed* rather than merely recorded; and what
happens when an observed value diverges from the governed one.

## Stage 3 — The reasoning (the full story)

**Read:** the [UIAO OrgPath reading sequence](../customer-documents/orgpath-narrative/index.qmd)
— twenty-nine books plus three supplements. If you read only a core: the
opening arc for the substrate story, and
[Book 18](../customer-documents/orgpath-narrative/Book_18.qmd) for why no
IGA platform (SailPoint, Saviynt, CyberArk, One Identity, Oracle, IBM,
Microsoft Entra) owns this gap. Beyond the Microsoft estate, the companion
[OrgPath for All Clouds](../customer-documents/orgpath-multicloud/index.qmd)
carries the same fifteen facets onto AWS, Google Cloud, Okta, LDAP, and
VMware.

**Do:** nothing to run — this stage is the *why* behind stages 1 and 2.

**Verify:** you can state the difference between the narrative's claim
(what the substrate is) and the implementation guides' claim (what ships
today), and where Substrate Status draws that line.

## Stage 4 — Run it (facets on a real tenant)

**Read:** the seven-step
[OrgPath Implementation Guides](../customer-documents/operational-guides/orgpath-implementation/index.qmd)
— the command-by-command path from an empty tenant to OrgPath facets on
Intune-managed devices and Azure Arc-enrolled servers, governed by a drift
loop. The guides target the GCC-Moderate boundary and are cloud-aware
(`--cloud commercial | gcc-high | dod`).

**Do:** work the guides in order against a test tenant — prerequisites
through operate-and-troubleshoot. (No tenant? The
[tier-1 setup guide](contributor-tier-1-setup.qmd) walks you to a free
Microsoft 365 Developer Program tenant.)

**Verify:** facets land on enrolled devices, and the drift loop surfaces a
deliberately introduced gap and classifies it. The guides say explicitly
where a capability is reserved rather than built — your deployment notes
should say the same.

## Stage 5 — The law (the lifecycle every change obeys)

**Read:** [One lifecycle, three pillars](../orgpath/index.qmd#macdr) — the
MACD-R authorized path (SSOT origination → authoritative authorization →
least-privilege execution with just-in-time elevation → closure with
provenance → verified evidence to continuous monitoring). Then the full
doctrine in
[OrgComp Vol 0 Book 00](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/Vol_0_Book_00_OrgComp_Executive_Summary.qmd#macdr-lifecycle),
including Closure Provenance and the per-class SSOT Registry.

**Do:** trace one joiner event and one leaver event through all five
clauses on paper — including what happens to the non-human identities
anchored to the leaver.

**Verify:** you can explain why "no closure counts unless it carries its
proof" is a governance invariant, not a reporting preference — and what an
ownerless service account is (an orphan finding, not a governed identity).

---

## Where this path leads

Operators who finish stage 5 are equipped to run the substrate against
their own environment and interpret its outputs — the competency the
canon's Training Program defines for its Operator track
([UIAO_125](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/specs/program-training.md)).
If your next step is federal compliance evidence, continue to the
[OrgComp Training Program](../customer-documents/orgcomp-series/OrgComp-Training-Program/index.qmd);
if it is moving a legacy estate, continue to the
[OrgMod path](orgmod-path.qmd).
